definitions.explanation: Skilled work done by hand, especially detailed or delicate work on objects. Also refers to the finished product of such work.
A clever or underhanded manipulation, tampering, or scheming done to achieve a desired outcome.

examples.japanese: {見事|みごと}な{細工|さいく}だ。
{金|きん}の{細工|さいく}が{施|ほどこ}された{箱|はこ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a box with gold filigree work on it.

examples.japanese: この{人形|にんぎょう}は{細工|さいく}が{細|こま}かくて{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: This doll has fine, detailed workmanship and is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {帳簿|ちょうぼ}に{細工|さいく}をした{疑|うたが}いがある。
examples.english: There is suspicion that the books were tampered with.

examples.japanese: いくら{細工|さいく}をしても、いずれ{真実|しんじつ}は{明|あき}らかになる。
examples.english: No matter how much you scheme, the truth will come to light eventually.

notes:
USAGE:
Used both as a standalone noun and in compounds. In sense 2, often appears with する to mean "to tamper with" or "to manipulate." The compound {小|こ}{細工|ざいく} (petty tricks) is very common and has a strongly negative connotation. Note the rendaku: さいく → ざいく in compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {細工|さいく}が{細|こま}かい: finely crafted
- {細工|さいく}を{施|ほどこ}す: to apply craftsmanship
- {細工|さいく}をする: to tamper with, to manipulate
- {小|こ}{細工|ざいく}: petty tricks, cheap tricks
- {竹|たけ}{細工|ざいく}: bamboo craft
- {金|きん}{細工|ざいく}: goldsmithing
